name: Dan (The place name Dan mentioned in Genesis 14:14, not a person)
title: The city of Dan – the northern border town of Israel
summary: Dan is a place name mentioned in Genesis 14:14, where Abraham pursued the enemies who had captured Lot all the way to Dan. The place later became known as the northernmost city of Israel, and the expression "from Dan to Be'er-Sheba" was used to describe the entire extent of the land. Although this is not a person, the place name is closely tied to Israel's history and geography throughout the Old Testament.

keyEvents.title: Abraham's pursuit to Dan
keyEvents.description: Abraham pursued the kings who had taken Lot captive all the way to Dan and defeated them there.

keyEvents.title: Spies from the tribe of Dan explore Laish
keyEvents.description: The Danites sent spies to explore Laish, which they later captured and renamed Dan.

keyEvents.title: The Danites conquer Laish and establish idol worship
keyEvents.description: The tribe of Dan conquered the city of Laish, called it Dan, and set up a carved image there.

keyEvents.title: Jeroboam's golden calf in Dan
keyEvents.description: King Jeroboam set up one of his two golden calves in Dan to prevent the people from going to Jerusalem to worship.

keyEvents.title: "From Dan to Be'er-Sheba" – an expression for all Israel
keyEvents.description: The expression "from Dan to Beersheba" was repeatedly used to describe the entire geographical extent of Israel from north to south.

keyEvents.title: Ben-Hadad's Attack on Dan
keyEvents.description: The Syrian king Ben-Hadad attacked and captured Dan along with other cities in northern Israel.
